Strike Threat Rises at Ports of L.A. and Long Beach

Plus: Target posts its strongest quarterly growth in years; and the Pentagon struggles to secure a critical material for Patriot missiles: rayon

By

A strike at the busiest U.S. container-port complex is possible as soon as Saturday, according to West Coast port employers, the WSJ Logistics Report’s Paul Berger writes.

The Pacific Maritime Association said Wednesday it was struggling to reach a labor deal with a union local that represents 250 security guards at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach ahead of the current contract’s expiration at 12:01 a.m. on Saturday.
